slides.title: A digital identity project with safe choices
body: Today: make a document or five-slide presentation for fictional River.
Bring together useful digital skills without publishing or revealing anyone’s personal details.
slides.prompt: What will make this more than a decorated profile?
slides.answer: Accurate useful content, demonstrated editing, a checked chart, safer choices and a saved/reopened file.
slides.notes: Adapted from Week 7 Digital Identity project/record. Removes real personal charts and automatic “banked UAS evidence” claims. This is a local formative review of taught skills, not accredited assessment.

slides.title: The skills we can now combine
body: Open and use a suitable tool; format with purpose; name, save and retrieve files.
Insert a visual without distortion; check data and explain a comparison.
Reduce unnecessary exposure and get help with a concerning online request.
slides.prompt: Which skills can the final file show, and which need a demonstration?
slides.answer: The file can show content/layout/chart; selecting, formatting, inserting and saving should also be observed or explained through a brief demonstration.
slides.notes: Do not infer all practical skills from an adult-completed template. Record the support provided and identify operations not yet observed.

slides.title: Choose one format and five sections
body: Choose GROW_W7_Digital_Identity_Starter.docx or the same-named .pptx starter.
Complete: safe introduction; interests; digital skills; what the data says; safer choices.
Use a document or five-slide deck. Both formats are assessed on the same six criteria.
slides.prompt: Does choosing a presentation mean you must speak to the class?
slides.answer: No. A private adult preview or written/pointed explanation is a valid review route.
slides.notes: Both starter formats have matching sections. Provide the practical record and complete River/source cards. A teacher-approved native-format copy is acceptable.

slides.title: What we know about River
body: River is a fictional display name for this classroom project. River enjoys drawing and model making.
No real surname, school, age, location, account or photograph is needed.
The data is the fictional club vote: Drawing 7, Model making 9, Coding 3, Gardening 5.
slides.prompt: Which information is enough for a general introduction?
slides.answer: The fictional display name, a classroom-simulation label and general interests.
slides.notes: Do not invite pupils to swap in their own online identity. Educational reflections on digital actions are permitted without adding identifying personal details.

slides.title: We do: chart plus a useful sentence
body: Insert your checked Week 5 chart or assets/GROW_Club_Votes_Chart.png.
Keep its proportions and readable labels; add “Fictional Makers Club votes” as a caption.
Write: “Model making received 9 votes, 2 more than Drawing.”
slides.prompt: What evidence supports the comparison?
slides.answer: The chart/table shows Model making 9 and Drawing 7; 9 − 7 = 2.
slides.notes: The supplied chart is a valid recovery resource. Record whether it was learner-created earlier or supplied. This review assesses accurate use/placement and reasoning, not unsupported claims of chart creation today.

slides.title: Write safer choices that can be used
body: For the prize/password message: pause, do not reply or follow its link, and ask an available adult.
For privacy: settings reduce exposure, but someone with access may still copy content.
Explain one of these limits accurately; no real account setting needs changing.
slides.prompt: Improve: “My profile is private, so it is completely safe.”
slides.answer: “Privacy settings can limit who sees content, but viewers may copy it. I should avoid unnecessary personal details and ask for help if worried.”
slides.notes: Do not ask for a pledge to publish positive posts. A valid project can recommend choosing not to post. No live report or safety investigation occurs.

slides.title: You do: complete and check the project
body: Replace all starter prompts and complete the five sections.
Demonstrate one useful formatting change and insert the chart image.
Add two actual digital actions used, an accurate comparison and practical safer choices.
slides.prompt: What would count as two digital actions?
slides.answer: For example: “I changed the heading size to make it readable” and “I reopened the saved file to check the final chart.”
slides.notes: Core actions can be demonstrated with accessible support. Avoid a personal skill claim that was not observed; use “practised with support” where appropriate.

slides.title: Review the same six things
body: Content, purposeful formatting, chart placement, data reasoning, safer choices, and file/review habits.
Show the evidence in the project. Your teacher will record support separately.
A supplied chart is allowed; say where it came from.
slides.prompt: Why is “I did everything independently” not a useful claim without evidence?
slides.answer: The practical actions and saved result need checking. Honest explanation of support helps identify a real next step.
slides.notes: Teacher local rubric totals 12: six criteria × up to 2 points. Criteria are given in teacher guidance/resource answers. No mark depends on private disclosure, public speaking or refusal of support.

slides.title: Save, reopen and improve one part
body: Save as GROW_W7_River_Digital_Identity_v1.docx or .pptx in the approved task folder.
Reopen the copy and check the five sections, chart and safer advice.
Make one useful edit, save again and explain its purpose.
slides.prompt: What would be a meaningful final edit?
slides.answer: Correct an inaccurate comparison, enlarge unreadable chart labels, improve a heading or replace an unsafe privacy promise.
slides.notes: If the final format is ODT/ODP, use the same base name and approved extension. Do not overwrite the supplied starter. Record one next learning step after the observed review.

slides.title: Show one skill and choose a next step
body: Choose one part to show privately or explain in writing, by pointing or with a scribe.
Complete: “I can show ___. Next I will practise ___. Support that would help is ___.”
slides.prompt: What matters about the next step?
slides.answer: It should be a small digital skill or checking action that can be practised and observed, with appropriate support.
slides.notes: Keep all work in approved classroom storage. No publishing, screenshots of accounts or automatic external evidence upload is part of this pack.

worksheet.title: A digital identity project with safe choices — practical record

tasks.heading: 1 · Plan the project from safe source material
tasks.prompt: Choose the document or presentation starter and plan its five sections using fictional River.
items: 1: Safe introduction — River; classroom simulation. 2: Interests — drawing and model making.
3: Digital skills — two actual editing/checking actions, described honestly.
4: Data — checked club chart, fictional-data caption and numerical comparison.
5: Safer choices — password/prize response and one realistic privacy/deletion limit.
tasks.answer: All five sections have a purpose and use the supplied fictional data. No real identity, location, credentials, photographs or personal online history are needed.

tasks.heading: 2 · Build the digital project
tasks.prompt: Open the chosen GROW_W7_Digital_Identity_Starter file. Complete all five sections and demonstrate the practical actions.
items: Make at least one purposeful formatting change that improves readability.
Insert your checked Week 5 chart or assets/GROW_Club_Votes_Chart.png; resize proportionally and add a factual caption.
State one accurate comparison using 7, 9, 3, 5 and label the data fictional.
Explain a safe response to the password/prize message plus a realistic privacy/deletion limit.
Save as GROW_W7_River_Digital_Identity_v1.docx/.pptx, or the approved native equivalent.
tasks.answer: Example comparison: Model making 9 leads Drawing 7 by 2. Example safety: do not send a password or follow the message link; tell an adult. Privacy settings limit exposure but cannot prevent every copy. The file shows readable sections and a legible undistorted chart.

tasks.heading: 3 · Reopen, improve and explain
tasks.prompt: Reopen the saved project. Use the six review headings to check your evidence. A private adult review is enough.
items: Content · formatting · chart placement · data reasoning · safer choices · file/review habits.
One useful change I made after review: ___. It helps because ___.
Chart source: my checked Week 5 chart / supplied pack chart.
Next digital skill to practise: ___. Support needed: ___.
tasks.answer: A meaningful improvement corrects an actual issue and is saved. State the chart source honestly. Example: enlarge the chart to read its labels, then save/reopen and check the comparison. A specific next step may be selecting a cell range or naming a new version.

worksheet.exit_question: How can the project demonstrate progress without claiming every skill was independent?
worksheet.exit_answer: Show the actual edits and checked file, describe the support used honestly and identify a specific next practice step.

preparation: Supply both matching project starters, the complete River source card and chart recovery PNG.
Check pupils can access their Week 5 work if using it; have the supplied chart ready so missing prior work does not block the project.
Prepare the six-criterion 12-point local review and a private demonstration route.
materials: River project/source cards and practical record

teacher.modelling: Model a chart insert, proportional resize and a factual caption, then compare 9 and 7 explicitly. Show how a readable heading change serves a purpose. Think aloud through one safer-choice sentence and demonstrate reopening the saved copy before review.
misconceptions: A completed template alone does not prove every operation was performed by the learner.
The supplied chart is permitted, but its source should be stated honestly.
Nine of 24 is not a majority.
A fictional profile demonstrates skills without disclosure.
A public presentation or external evidence upload is not necessary.
teacher.support: Offer the same five sections in the pupil’s preferred format, one section at a time. Use short source prompts and accessible input; adults may scribe explanations while observing the learner’s digital actions. Support does not automatically reduce concept marks.
teacher.stretch: Ask the learner to explain a misleading data claim or a privacy overpromise, improve the information order, or demonstrate how preserving the starter and choosing a version name supports later retrieval.
teacher.fallback: Create a paper storyboard with five sections and the supplied numeric chart information. Record planning, reasoning and safety understanding. Do not award unobserved digital-operation points; schedule those checks when a device is available.
teacher.safeguarding: Use fictional River and supplied counts only. Do not include real identifying details, account information, credentials or personal online experiences. Nothing is sent, published or uploaded. Handle any disclosure privately using the school safeguarding route.
teacher.assessment: Local formative review, maximum 12: six criteria scored 0–2. Content: 1 for at least three meaningful sections, 2 for all five accurate sections. Formatting: 1 for a demonstrated useful text-format edit, 2 when the resulting structure is consistently readable. Chart placement: 1 for inserting a correct chart, 2 when proportion, labels and factual caption remain clear. Data reasoning: 1 for a correct count, 2 for an accurate numerical comparison with fictional-data context. Safer choices: 1 for one useful safe action, 2 for a practical password-message response plus an accurate privacy/deletion limit. File/review: 1 for a sensibly named saved copy, 2 for reopening the intended copy and making/explaining a saved improvement. Score 0 where that criterion is not demonstrated. Record support separately; supplied-chart use is allowed. Revisit unsafe advice or personal-data inclusion before considering the project ready, regardless of total. This is not accredited assessment.

resources.title: River’s complete project brief and review cards
resources.instructions: Choose document or slides. Complete the same five sections using only this fictional material. Use the six review criteria on the cards to check the final file; no public sharing is required.

Review B · Chart placement: inserted correct chart with clear proportions/labels/caption. Data reasoning: accurate count and numerical comparison using fictional context.

Scoring: six criteria, 0–2 each, maximum 12. Content 1 = three meaningful sections, 2 = all five accurate. Formatting 1 = useful demonstrated edit, 2 = readable consistent result. Chart 1 = correct insert, 2 = proportion/labels/caption clear.

Data 1 = correct count, 2 = accurate comparison plus fictional context. Safety 1 = one useful safe action, 2 = password response plus privacy/deletion limit. Files 1 = named saved copy, 2 = reopen/check plus saved explained improvement. Zero = not demonstrated.
